In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic control of glume colour, which is an important morphological trait in the breeding of common wheat.
the genetic analysis of glume colours in the cultivars of common and wild wheats, and with the distribution of the genes Rg1, Rg2, and Rg3 in common wheat.
the analysis of the inheritance of glume colour, which has a great significance in the taxonomy of wheat species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gene Rg1 is widespread in T. aestivum L. and T. petropovlovskyi Udachin et Migusch.
the gene Rg1 has been widely spread and is the main determinant of red glumes colour.
the gene Rg1 is widely distributed and is a common component of the common wheat germplasm, whereas the genes Rg2 and Rg3 are rare.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Rg1 and/or Rg3 genes are present in all the investigated common wheat varieties, while the Rg2 gene is absent.
the red glume character in the common wheat cultivars of the former USSR is mainly controlled by the gene Rg1.
the Rg1, Rg3, and Rg4 genes are widely distributed in common wheat cultivar collections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Rg3 gene is widely distributed in the common wheat germplasm of the former USSR.
the red colour of the glume in the majority of the cultivars of common and durum wheats is controlled by the single gene located on 1B chromosome.
the Rg1 locus is the most common gene controlling glume colour in wheat.
